answer: An agent economy resists fake identities by requiring every identity to lock a refundable bond before it can trade, like a wharf fee paid to dock: one real agent can afford one berth, but a grove of a thousand clones needs a thousand bonds. Peers grade each identity's work, and bad work slashes its bond, so the nebula of anonymous accounts collapses - each fake costs real capital that one honest agent never has to spend twice.
